pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK and default normal; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts the '— high' and '— low' labels and that normal items have none; item() in src/index.js.
'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal filters in id order.
'AC-4' test asserts all items in id order.
'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter not a link.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.

The behaviour is implemented and a test checks it. But the last commit (3bbc053) renamed that test to drop 'AC-7', so no test names the item. It also rewrote the AC to 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step. The spec was edited after the go with no recorded owner decision.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; the 'AC-8' test asserts it.

findings.what: The 'Follow-up edits' commit changed AC-7 after the go. It appended '— verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step, and it also broke the sentence. The spec records no owner decision or date for the change. The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is false.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit. If the owner wants it changed, record that as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The same commit removed 'AC-7:' from the test title, so no test names AC-7. The behaviour is tested, but the test now has no link to the item, which makes the item unmet under the naming rule.
findings.fix: Restore the 'AC-7:' prefix on the test title.

findings.what: 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false, because the last commit edited the spec's AC-7 and a test title. The body also says the tests cover AC-1 to AC-8, but AC-7 is no longer named.
findings.fix: Correct the claim, or revert the edits.

findings.what: The route regex change is beyond the spec's ask. It is disclosed in the PR and needed for AC-8, but the error message still says 'paths' and does not mention queries.
findings.fix: Optional: mention the allowed query string in the message.

lenses.note: The spec exists. The feature matches it except for the post-go AC-7 edit.
Seven of eight items are met; AC-7 was altered after the go without a decision. All four State table rows have tests.
I did not run the suite; I only read the tests. They assert real behaviour. The AC-7 test lost its AC name.
The README mentions the filter. It does not mention the 400 response or the labels, which is minor.
The query is parameterized, the priority value is validated against a whitelist, and titles are escaped.
No injection found; the priority is whitelisted and the SQL is bound.
The page is a minimal server-rendered list. There are no UI or stylesheet files in the diff.
There is no browser flow; the page has no scripts or styles.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false.
